name: section-data-context
body:
Next to the existing rendered-HTML list for each declared section, a layout receives the same authored instances as DATA under the reserved `.data` context: `.data.<section>` is a list with one entry per authored instance of that declared section, in source order, and each entry carries `.raw` (that instance's original source field values), `.item` (its sibling descriptor, item-context) and `.data` (its own child-section data, keyed the same way) — so the whole authored section tree is addressable as data. The rendered-HTML list under `.sectionName` is unchanged and remains the value a layout ranges over to splice markup; `.data` is the parallel data view. `.data` is data, not a helper (exposing it adds nothing to the layout function set) and `data` is a reserved top-level name: a template declaring a field or section named `data` is a templates error (requirements.constraint.reserved-template-names, domain.constraint.template-context-reserved). A section invoked by the `section` helper is a direct render call, not an authored instance of a declared section, so it does not append an entry to the caller's `.data`; the target template still sees its own `.raw` and its own children's `.data`.

AC: for a slide with two `blocks` instances, `{{ len .data.blocks }}` is 2 and `{{ range .data.blocks }}{{ .raw.text }}{{ end }}` yields the two source field values while `{{ range .blocks }}{{ . }}{{ end }}` still splices their rendered HTML; a nested instance's children are reached through the entry's own `.data`; `.data` is data, not a layout function; loading a template that declares a field or section named `data` is a templates error.
